first:
You asked for the blue cord, and I stepped onto my ferry. As I did so, I could feel Nera Moss’ gaze upon me, her heart heavy with anticipation.
What is this place? A harbor of unknown might. It’s clear to me that we have only a short time left before our destination. It feels like we’ve been living in this town for seven years, too long to be just simple curiosity.

We are now navigating towards what will be a new journey, filled with many secrets yet to be discovered. What does it take to leave our familiar world behind? This is what makes our lives so unique. Not every journey is meant for death. But we must find out, or else we'll never know the full story.
retry:
You step onto the ferry, and I ask you what you want to do. You look at me with curiosity, and a twinge of anticipation. But first, I must navigate through the world.

You are in Bellwether, waiting for your next adventure. What will it be? We have been here for many years, but we know nothing about this place or people who live there. This is not like any other town or harbor, but something unique.

You gaze out the window, looking into the water. It looks calm, but there's an eerie silence that draws you closer. The harbor has no walls or docks; everything floats on its own, and it seems as though the tide itself moves along.

Suddenly, you hear the sound of footsteps approaching. It’s Mara Vale, the cartographer returning from her journey. Her eyes widen when she realizes what you’ve just said, and she stops abruptly, staring at the waves before turning around and looking away.

“You came,” she says. “Good.” She turns around and goes to greet you. As she approaches, you can see that she hasn’t left your side yet, so you feel a bit awkward about asking her for help.

“Hey, I need some instructions,” you say, trying to find your footing. As she turns around, you can see that she hasn't moved at all since she arrived. She continues to stare at the sea, looking around at the small town and the ocean horizon.

"You don’t have a compass," Mara Vale admits, still staring at the sea. She shakes her head, nodding her head, showing a little smile, then continuing her stare at the sea. You wonder if she remembers anything or knows anything about these strange waters, but what really annoys you more is that you haven’t had time to talk to her about what you saw.

You notice a faint breeze, and you can tell Mara Vale isn’t faring well. Her surroundings aren’t clear, and she looks lost. As you move further, she disappears into the horizon, leaving behind a ghostly memory of what was once known to watch her over the horizon.

“Hey, could you give me a ride?” you ask, moving forward again. You realize Mara Vale didn’t leave her after all, but now she’s gone. You can only assume she’s lost herself, but maybe she went for a ride because she needed something else? It doesn’t make sense, but you couldn’t deny that feeling of being lost. You look at Mara Vale, who is now gone, and you realize that she might have been one of those people who lived in the past, who wasn’t aware of the depths of their oceans, who didn’t have dreams.
accepted: Nera Moss gives Mara Vale the blue cord. Mara ties the blue cord around her wrist. Nera and Mara depart Bellwether aboard the ferry.
